scope: Immutable container build inputs, commit-pinned workflow actions, non-publishing OCI release-candidate construction, vulnerability gating, SBOMs, checksums, and signed provenance

priorRisk.control: Exact human-readable container tags without immutable digests
priorRisk.failureMode: A publisher could move an upstream tag and change an application, CI-service, or local-development input without a ReconAI source change.

implementedControls: the Dockerfile frontend and every external FROM input retain a readable tag plus reviewed manifest-list SHA-256 digest
all five Compose services use readable tags plus immutable manifest-list digests
GitHub Actions PostgreSQL, Redis, and Docker-run MinIO inputs use immutable manifest-list digests
all external workflow actions are pinned to full commit SHAs
pnpm container:check is included in pnpm verify and rejects unreviewed container repositories or pin regressions
the validator rejects registry login, image push, registry-attestation push, package/repository/deployment write permission, and release creation in the candidate workflow
the candidate workflow is manually dispatched, main-branch-only, and requires the exact BUILD-NON-PUBLISHING-CANDIDATE confirmation
the candidate grants only contents read, OIDC token, attestation write, and artifact-metadata write
each application candidate is a local linux/amd64 OCI archive with BuildKit maximum provenance and SBOM
Trivy is configured to reject fixed High/Critical operating-system or library vulnerabilities and emit an external CycloneDX SBOM
SHA-256 checksums bind the OCI archive and external SBOM
actions/attest v4.2.0 is commit-pinned and configured for signed SLSA provenance plus an SBOM attestation over the candidate archive
candidate archives, checksums, SBOMs, and attestation bundles are retained for 30 days without registry, release, or deployment authority

checks: exact dependency-policy validation across 20 package manifests
production builds across all applicable workspace projects, including Next.js

registryResolution.method: Authenticated anonymous pull metadata from the official Docker Hub and Quay Registry V2 APIs
registryResolution.interpretation: The recorded digests and platform sets were observed from the official registries on the review date. This proves the tag-to-manifest mapping at that instant, not publisher trust or ongoing vulnerability status.

workflowYamlParsing.interpretation: The YAML parser accepted each document and the repository validator inspected semantic values. actionlint and the GitHub hosted runner were unavailable.

unverified: Dockerfile frontend and base-image pull by digest
application image build and runtime behavior
OCI archive export and embedded BuildKit provenance/SBOM
Trivy image vulnerability gate and CycloneDX generation
GitHub OIDC/Sigstore provenance and SBOM attestation
artifact retention and downloaded checksum/gh attestation verification
repository visibility or plan eligibility for artifact attestations

operationalImpact.baseImageUpgradeBehavior: Upstream tag movement no longer changes a build; security updates require a reviewed source digest change.
operationalImpact.rollback: Replace an unsuitable digest with a separately reviewed digest. Do not restore mutable tag-only container inputs or remove artifact identity verification.

remainingEvidenceAndOperationalRisks: Run the candidate workflow from main in an authorized repository whose visibility or plan supports GitHub artifact attestations.
Inspect all three archive builds, embedded BuildKit provenance/SBOMs, Trivy results, external CycloneDX SBOMs, checksum manifests, signed bundles, source commits, and workflow identities.
Download each candidate and pass sha256sum --check plus gh attestation verify against the expected owner/repository identity.
Define and review supported production platforms; the current candidate is linux/amd64 only.
After explicit owner publication approval, define a protected registry and bind image-level attestations to the exact published image digest.
Enforce expected signer/repository/workflow identity and immutable digest verification before any staging or production deployment.
Exercise container startup, non-root runtime, health checks, Compose networking, staging rollout, rollback, and admission failure paths.
Continue reviewed digest refreshes because immutable pins intentionally do not receive upstream security updates automatically.
No hosted image build, vulnerability scan, signed attestation, registry publication, staging deployment, or production result is claimed.
